learningObjective: Identify correct and incorrect statements about host/device synchronization in a CUDA-based ML runtime.

canonicalClaims.claim: cudaStreamSynchronize waits only for the specified stream; cudaDeviceSynchronize waits for all streams on the current device. Overusing the latter in a hot loop defeats stream-based overlap.
conditions: Legacy default-stream semantics unless per-thread default stream is enabled.
nonImplications: Does not imply cudaStreamSynchronize is always cheap; a heavily loaded stream can force long waits.
Does not imply device sync should never be used; it is appropriate at process shutdown or measurement boundaries.

misconceptions.claim: cudaMemcpyAsync automatically overlaps with kernels on other streams.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Overlap requires pinned host memory and correct stream separation; async alone is not sufficient.

misconceptions.claim: The default stream is independent of user-created streams under legacy semantics.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Under legacy default stream, all user streams synchronize with the default stream.

misconceptions.claim: cudaDeviceSynchronize is a no-op when only one stream is active.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It always waits for all outstanding device work regardless of stream count.
cudaMemcpy is blocking with respect to the host thread and synchronizes with prior work.
